async def act(page):
    """
    From the current Manage Products grid, filter the product list for "Frankie Sweatshirt"
    and open its Edit page. The final action (clicking Edit) navigates away, so it is done last.
    """
    # Wait for the page to be idle
    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")

    # Find the product table (the table that contains the header link "Name")
    product_table = page.get_by_role("table").filter(has=page.get_by_role("link", name="Name"))

    # Fill the Name filter textbox with the product name (scoped to the product table)
    name_filter = product_table.get_by_role("textbox", name="Name")
    await name_filter.fill("Frankie Sweatshirt")

    # Click the Search button using the full table->cell path for the Reset Filter / Search controls
    search_button = (
        product_table
        .get_by_role("cell", name="Reset Filter Search")
        .get_by_role("button", name="Search")
    )
    await search_button.click()

    # Wait for the grid to update
    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")

    # Find the product row that contains the link "Frankie Sweatshirt" and click its Edit link (navigates away)
    product_row = (
        product_table
        .get_by_role("row")
        .filter(has=page.get_by_role("link", name="Frankie Sweatshirt"))
    )

    edit_link = product_row.get_by_role("link", name="Edit")
    await edit_link.click()

3) I scoped the Name filter textbox to the product table to avoid ambiguity and filled it with "Frankie Sweatshirt" so the grid will be filtered to the product we need to edit.

4) I located the Search button using the full path through the table cell labeled "Reset Filter Search" to follow the guidance about using full .get_by_role() paths for ambiguous controls, then clicked it and waited for the grid to update.

5) After the results update, I locate the table row that contains the link "Frankie Sweatshirt" and click its Edit link. This click is expected to navigate away to the product edit page, so it is performed as the last action in act().

6) No knowledge-base functions were used because none were available; I considered them but found none relevant.
